newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche - no decision yet on branch revamp.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche - no decision yet on branch revamp.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Tuesday it was continuing to mull changes to its domestic branch network but had not taken final decisions yet.
A spokesman for Germany's largest bank dismissed as "speculation" recent media reports that the bank planned to close half of its 16 main branches in a streamlining of its branch network.
The bank already denied a similar report last month.

The Frankfurt Allgemeine Zeitung reported that Deutsche would soon decide on a reorganisation of its branches and that the issue would be on the agenda of a regular management board meeting on Tuesday.

The bank spokesman said: "It is true that the management of our bank is dealing with the further development of our branch structure. But all sides involved have to be included in the decision-making process."
The spokesman said he could not give a date when a decision would be reached.

Deutsche, like most of Germany's commercial banks, is seeking to woo customers and improve profitability in its domestic retail banking business by extending branch opening hours as well as offering telephone and computer banking.
Deutsche also recently opened its first branch in a supermarket.
